Attribution

/at-ruh-BYOO-shun/ · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Attribution means the act of assigning a cause, source, or credit to someone or something.

Attribution means the act of assigning a cause, source, or credit to someone or something. The museum revised its attribution of the unsigned portrait after pigment tests pointed to a different painter's workshop.

Worked Example

After a record flood, reporters wanted to know whether a warming climate was to blame. A research team simulated the same storm in model worlds with and without warmer oceans, then published a careful attribution of the disaster, assigning about a third of the extra rainfall to the warming and the rest to an unlucky alignment of weather patterns. Their task was not to praise or accuse anyone, but to assign the right share of the outcome to the right cause.

The scientists formally assigned shares of the flood to specific causes, and that act of assigning is exactly what attribution means.

How Attribution Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

ascription

ascription: the assigning of something to a source or cause

crediting

crediting: the act of naming who is responsible for something

Antonyms

disavowal

disavowal: a formal denial of connection or responsibility

How Strong Is It? — speculation → verdict → attribution

speculation vs. attribution

speculation vs. attribution: Speculation merely guesses at where something came from, while an attribution formally assigns it to a source or cause.

verdict vs. attribution

verdict vs. attribution: An attribution assigns responsibility based on evidence, but a verdict makes that assignment official and binding.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of attribution.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — at-

Prefix — at-: a form of ad-, to or toward

Root — tribu

Root — tribu: from Latin tribuere, to assign or allot, originally to divide among the tribes

Suffix — -tion

Suffix — -tion: the act or process of

Put it together

Put it together: Attribution comes from Latin attribuere, 'to assign to,' built on tribuere, 'to allot or divide,' a verb the Romans first used for dividing things among the tribus, or tribes. An attribution literally allots a work, quality, or cause to its proper owner.

Use the root in a new word: contribute

Use the root in a new word: contribute: Everyone who chips in to the class gift contributes, literally allotting a share together, from the same Latin root tribuere.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal, academic/journalistic register

Attribution takes 'of' for the thing assigned and 'to' for its source (the attribution of the quote to Twain). It covers credit, blame, and cause alike: scientists speak of the attribution of a heat wave to a warming climate just as editors speak of the attribution of a quotation to its speaker.
